Before ordering, decide K1 (set-in vs dropped shoulder) and say whether the jacket in the visual chart has a dropped shoulder. The 50 cm shoulder makes sense only for the construction it was measured on.

Give the factory this document. Require: the provisional target range for chest, shoulder and body length; Golden Bear's method definitions (§4) for every POM; and a sleeve length set on the fit model, not taken from either chart.
Require the factory to return the measured spec of the prototype using the §10 checklist, with each POM's method written down, plus the flat photos with a ruler.
Keep A as a fallback: buy a Golden Bear Classic M only if the prototype misses the target range in a way that can't be explained, or if the factory can't measure to the documented methods.

conversionToFactoryCm: Inputs locked per size after physical approval: zone box W × H (cm), zone centre from the primary anchor (Y) and secondary anchor (X).
Customer data per element (already stored): artwork aspect a = width / height; inZone = { scale s ∈ [0.2, 1], x, y } (shares of the box, x → right and y → up, facing the zone).
Auto-fit size: if a ≥ W / H then w₀ = W, h₀ = W / a; else h₀ = H, w₀ = H × a.
Finished artwork size: w = w₀ × s, h = h₀ × s (cm).
Customer offset from zone centre: ΔX = x × W, ΔY = y × H (cm, facing the zone). The software already clamps x, y so the artwork stays inside the box.

Artwork centre on the garment: Y below anchor = zone Y − ΔY. Body zones: X from CF/CB = zone X ± ΔX (front: + toward wearer's left as faced; back: mirrored). Sleeve zones: ΔX runs around the sleeve from its outer centre line.
Rotation: not supported in fixed zones (always 0).

Versioning: orders store physicalSize and referencePosition computed from the 3D boxes; once physical zones are approved, each order should record which zone-spec version it was produced against, so old orders are never re-interpreted.
Open decision: zones are the same for every size today. Whether physical zone positions/boxes grade by size or stay fixed is a pattern-maker decision (no source documents graded placement).

why: Golden Bear supplies the set-in shoulder width and its grading; the dropped shoulder moves the shoulder point outwards by the extension on each side.
